Install, maintain, and repair telemetry systems and recording and metering devices.
Support safe operation of hydroelectric units, performing startup/shutdown, synchronization, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), clearances, and routine/emergency switching at system voltages.
Install, test, and maintain protective relays, control circuits, excitation systems, Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) interfaces, and interpret drawings and logic diagrams.
Maintain motors, Motor Control Centers (MCCs), battery systems, grounding grids, lighting circuits, HVAC electrical systems, and perform preventive maintenance on auxiliary systems.
Follow Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), National Fire Protection Association’s (NFPA) 70E/dam safety rules; perform arc-flash assessments, hazard analyses, emergency response, and complete accurate documentation and reports.
EXPERIENCE: A specific length of training and experience is not required, but you must show evidence of training or experience of sufficient scope and quality of your ability to do the work of this position.

Evidence which demonstrates you possess the knowledge, skills, and ability to perform the duties of this position must be supported by detailed descriptions of such on your resume. Applicants will be rated in accordance with the OPM Qualification Standard Handbook Federal Wage System Qualifications.

SCREEN-OUT ELEMENT: Your qualifications will first be evaluated against the prescribed screen out element. Those applicants who appear to possess at least the minimal acceptable qualification requirement are considered for further rating; those who do not are rated ineligible and are eliminated.

Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the job elements and screen out listed below: 1. Ability to do the work of the position without more than normal supervision. (SCREEN OUT) (OPM Job Element 1) 2. Knowledge of Electrical Equipment (OPM Job Element 2B) 3.

Theory of Instruments (electrical, electronic) used in Shop and Trade Practices (OPM Job Element 25-D) 4. Ability to Use and Maintain Hand tools (OPM Job Element 81-B) 5. Troubleshooting (Electrical) (OPM Job Element 96A) 6.

Ability to Use Electrical Drawings (OPM Job Element 75J) If your knowledge and ability in the SCREEN OUT factor above is not sufficient, you will receive no further consideration.

In preparing your application, describe in detail the experience and training which you have had that specifically prepared you for this job and to perform the duties described for this job. Experience should be clearly described and documented in your resume.

The qualifications reviewer will not assume performance of such duties by Job Titles alone. Address your knowledge, skills and/or abilities in the areas shown in the job related factors. Minimum qualifications for trades and labor positions are determined by evaluation of job elements.

You must meet at least 2 points on the screen-out element(s) and obtain an average of at least 2 points on all of the job elements in order to be considered qualified for this position.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Physical Efforts and Working Conditions: Work requires heavy physical exertion.

The work involves unassisted lifting and carrying of items weighing over forty-five pounds or up to fifty pounds (i.e., tools and equipment components); pulling and pushing of two- and four-wheel carts loaded with tools and equipment weighing up to two hundred pounds; prolonged standing; recurring climbing flights of stairs; and climbing and working on ladders and scaffolding up to 254 feet.

Duties also involve operating a pick-up truck, one-ton truck, and a 24,000-pound GVW bucket truck. The position requires sufficient hearing acuity to discern equipment noises and normal visual acuity to read diagrams, technical documents, and manuals.

Work is performed in physically tight spaces requiring prolonged kneeling and squatting; below ground in dam corridors to depths of up to 263 feet; on high structures including cranes on the dam up to 254 feet; and above water at the dam intake and the powerhouse transformer deck.

Works indoors and outdoors in all types of weather conditions and temperature extremes. Exposed to high and constant noise levels from diesel generators, sandblasting equipment, hydroelectric turbines, and generators.

Exposed to heat, extensive dust from sandblasting, contaminated air from diesel exhaust and welding fumes, and dangerous chemicals such as alcohol, battery acid, and cleaning solvents.

Subject to electrical burns and shock from generating and electrical distribution equipment; and to falls from slippery, wet, and uneven walking surfaces at the dam penstocks and valves.

Exposed to eye hazards from dust, welding, and grinding particles; and to injury from machinery with dangerous moving parts including drills, saws, various machine shop equipment, and machinery in motion very close to the incumbent such as motor shafts, pumps, and compressors.

Requires the use of protective devices such as ear plugs, safety hats, non-conductive gloves and footwear, and similar protective gear. The occasional use of a self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) or face-fitted respirator may be required following a medical examination to determine any limitations.

Work may occur below ground in dam corridors to depths of fifty feet, on high structures including cranes on the dam (up to 254 feet), and above water at the dam intake and the powerhouse transformer deck.

Here at The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit and that can carry cargo - and potentially humans in the longer run.
To support this ambitious goal, we are seeking an Electrical Test Technician to join our Electrical Integration & Test Team in Munich. You will be responsible for the assembly, integration, maintenance, and modification of electrical test systems used throughout the development, verification, and validation of spacecraft subsystems and avionics equipment.
You will play a key role in building and maintaining custom test racks, integrating commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) and custom-designed hardware, and supporting engineers during test campaigns. Working closely with electrical, avionics, and system engineers, you will help ensure our test infrastructure meets the highest standards of quality, reliability, and safety.

s.h: In your role as Electrical Test Technician, you will
s.t:
Assemble, wire, and integrate electrical test racks and ground support equipment
Perform wiring and interconnections between COTS equipment and custom-designed hardware
Manufacture, route, label, and install electrical harnesses and cables according to engineering documentation
Interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical drawings to perform integration and troubleshooting activities
Support electrical integration, verification, and test campaigns across multiple projects
Perform inspections, modifications, and repairs on electrical assemblies and test equipment
Assist in the installation, replacement, and rework of electronic components on PCBs when required
Execute continuity, insulation, and basic electrical verification tests on assemblies and harnesses
Maintain accurate documentation of wiring modifications, test setups, and configuration changes
Support troubleshooting and root-cause investigations on electrical and test systems

s.h: You and your team will be in charge of
s.t:
Building and maintaining reliable electrical test infrastructures for spacecraft development and qualification activities
Integrating a wide variety of electrical equipment, including power supplies, measurement devices, automation components, and custom electronics
Ensuring all rack assemblies and wiring installations comply with internal standards and safety requirements
Supporting engineers during test setup preparation, execution, and troubleshooting activities
Contributing to the continuous improvement of test equipment, assembly processes, and documentation practices
Maintaining high levels of workmanship, quality, and configuration control across all electrical integration activities
Ensuring electrical installations are safe, maintainable, and suitable for demanding aerospace test environments

Technical diploma, vocational qualification, or equivalent experience in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, Mechatronics, Industrial Automation, or a related field
Proven hands-on experience in electrical assembly, wiring, and integration activities
Ability to read, interpret, and work from electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical documentation
Experience assembling and wiring electrical cabinets, racks, or industrial control systems
Knowledge of cable and wire selection principles, including preliminary conductor sizing based on electrical loads and installation constraints
Familiarity with common industrial automation components such as relays, contactors, circuit breakers, terminal blocks, sensors, power supplies, and I/O modules
Experience using standard electrical test equipment, including multimeters, oscilloscopes, power supplies, and continuity testers
Strong troubleshooting skills and a structured, methodical approach to problem-solving
High attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship
Fluent in English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills
Ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary engineering teams in a fast-paced environment
Nice-to-Have Skills
Experience with aerospace, automotive, railway, or other highly regulated industries
Experience performing PCB assembly, component replacement, soldering, and electronic rework
Familiarity with low-voltage DC power distribution systems
Knowledge of cable harness manufacturing and connector assembly standards
Experience working with custom-built test equipment and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) environments
Ability to design rack front panels and front-end layouts for custom test systems
Familiarity with CAD tools for electrical or mechanical design documentation
Understanding of configuration management and documentation control processes

Du bist mitverantwortlich für die komplette temporäre Stromversorgung auf verschiedenen Baustellen und Infrastrukturprojekten.

🏗️ Was diesen Job besonders macht

At Sunrun, we're on a mission to change the way the world interacts with energy, and we're building a company and brand that puts power at the center of life. To do it, we're designing a dynamic culture where employee development, well-being, and safety come first. It's why we've become the #1 home solar and battery company in America.

We're unlike any other residential energy company. Our vertically integrated model gives us total control over every part of the energy lifecycle - from sale through installation and beyond - so you can find endless opportunities for growth. Come join a career you can grow in and a culture you can run with.
Who We Are
We're on a mission to make energy more reliable and affordable for more people. We provide an opportunity with storage and solar to help people access greater energy independence without the big upfront costs. Sunrun is the largest dedicated residential solar and storage company in the country and has a mission to bring stably priced resilient power to the masses.
About Sunrun
Since 2007, Sunrun has grown into America's #1 home solar and battery company. We got here by putting our people's safety and growth first. That's why we created the Power+ program: to invest in your skills.

Your are responsible for on-site inspection, maintenance and repair of electrical and electronic equipment and facilities and electrical and electronic features of structures and mechanical equipment.
You will perform work at at a multiple purpose hydroelectric dam, spillway, hydroelectric power generating plant and switchyard.
You will check the operation of all equipment in order to detect abnormal conditions and correct them before they become serious. You will test repaired equipment to assure proper performance.
You will plan work operations consistent with broad work schedules based on urgency of repair, interference with other operations, availability of equipments and personnel, and time required to complete work.
You will provide technical guidance to Journeymen Electrician and Power Plant Trainees.
You will maintain records and data in connection with all electrical maintenance and repair work.
You will plan and perform installation of new electrical equipment on primary and auxiliary power plant systems.
You will respond to callouts and independently perform assessments of equipment to diagnose problems and develop repair plans. You will strictly adhere to safety standards to include compliance with Hazardous Energy Control Plan procedures.

Minimum Qualifications (Screen Out Element): Ability to do the work of a(n) POWER PLANT SENIOR ELECTRICIAN, WB-2810-00 without more than normal supervision; this will involve at least the performance of common preventative maintenance, testing and repairs on electrical and electronic equipment at multi-purpose hydroelectric dam, hydroelectric power generating plant, spillway, intake structure, or switchyard..

Failure to meet this Screen Out Element will result in an ineligible rating. Also, you will be evaluated on other Job Elements which are listed below.

Ability To Do The Work Of The position Without More Than Normal Supervision Ability To Use and Maintain Hand Tools (Electrical Work) Ability To Use Electrical Drawings Knowledge of Electrical Equipment Technical Practices (theoretical, precise, artistic) Theory and Instruments (Electrical Electronic) Used in Shop and Trade Practices Trouble shooting (electrical) PHYSICAL EFFORT: Work tasks require that the incumbent be capable of rapid simultaneous mental and muscular coordination in conjunction with eye and hand coordination to operate switches and controls in accordance with meter indications.

Machine work, welding, soldering and other specialized tasks require dexterity and the use of both hands.

In order to perform the maintenance, inspection and operation of power station equipment, the incumbent must be able to lift and carry heavy objects of 45 pounds and over, climb ladders, reach above the shoulders, stand, sit, crawl and kneel for prolonged periods and perform repeated bending.

To use power plant communications, normal speech and hearing are necessary. To recognize color codes, incumbent must have normal correctable vision and normal color vision. The incumbent must be able to operate cranes and motor vehicles. Climb stairs and capable of sensing and responding to audible and visual alarms without the use of aid devices.

WORKING CONDITIONS: The incumbent will work primarily inside around machinery in operation; in close proximity to high and low voltage circuits and climbs stairs frequently.

Sometimes work will be performed outside in weather of varying degree of temperature and humidity, in tight or cramped (confined) work spaces, below ground, above water, at heights, on ladders or scaffolds, and on slippery or uneven walking surfaces.

Occasionally the incumbent will use solvents, degreasing agents, or other chemical agents, and be assigned to protracted or irregular hours of work; use both hands in water and is exposed to silica, dust, asbestos, oil, grease, constant or excessive noise, vibration, and smoke and gas fumes.

Working around machinery with moving parts, moving objects, and moving vehicles is to be expected. The incumbent will be working closely with others and/or alone depending on assigned daily activities. Personal protective safety devices will be supplied to the worker when in an area of hazardous exposure.

Examples of devices are hard hats, safety shoes, safety goggles and glasses fresh air breathing masks, gloves, dust and smoke respirators, ear muffs, insulated gloves and safety grounds. When in an area of hazardous exposure, the incumbent will wear the appropriate personal safety device.

Must wear supplied Arc Flash rated clothing at all times while working within the facility.

The incumbent ensures the efficient accomplishment of work by subordinates so that new equipment is installed in a way it can be maintained. This position is essential. The incumbent is required to report to work during emergencies and inclement weather situations. The tour of duty will include weekends, evenings and holidays on a regular and recurring basis. Tour of duty may be other than Monday through Friday.

Recommends modification and/or replacement of parts that are no longer available through procurement procedures. Battery systems and their associated charging systems. Maintains D.C. supervisory and pilot circuits, maintains emergency lighting. Conducts regular surveys and tours to determine existing layout and condition of work areas, facility conditions, and system operational status. Troubleshoots electrical components under live conditions.

Performs repairs and adjustments that are often complicated by critical tolerance and the extremely delicate nature of the components.

## **Ta mission :** ##
### Réaliser des installations électriques en environnement industriel ###
Vous participez à la réalisation d-installations électriques en **courant fort et courant faible (CFO/CFA)** sur des sites industriels, dans le respect des plans, des normes suisses, des règles de sécurité et des exigences du projet.
### Intervenir en environnement ATEX ###
Vous intervenez dans des zones à risques d-atmosphères explosives. **La formation ATEX est obligatoire** pour ce poste. Vous appliquez les procédures et règles de sécurité spécifiques aux environnements ATEX.
### Installer et raccorder les équipements ###
Vous assurez le tirage et le raccordement des câbles, la pose des équipements électriques ainsi que l-installation des chemins de câbles et infrastructures nécessaires.
### Lire et interpréter les plans ###
Vous analysez les plans et schémas électriques afin de garantir des installations conformes, fiables et de qualité.
### Contribuer à la réussite des chantiers ###
En collaboration avec les équipes, vous participez au bon déroulement des travaux et veillez au respect des délais, de la qualité et des règles de sécurité.
## **Maintenant si on parlait de toi ?** ##
### Une solide formation technique ###
Vous êtes titulaire d-un **CFC d-installateur-électricien, de monteur-électricien** ou d-un diplôme équivalent reconnu en Suisse.
### Une expérience en environnement industriel ###
Vous disposez d-une expérience confirmée dans le domaine électrique, idéalement acquise sur des **sites industriels**.
### Une formation ATEX obligatoire ###
Vous êtes **titulaire d-une formation ATEX à jour** et connaissez les règles de sécurité liées aux atmosphères explosibles.
### De bonnes compétences techniques ###
Vous maîtrisez le **CFO/CFA**, la lecture de plans, le tirage de câbles, les raccordements, l-appareillage et la pose de chemins de câbles.
La connaissance des **normes NIBT** et une expérience du marché suisse sont des atouts importants.
### Un professionnel fiable et rigoureux ###
Autonome, consciencieux et impliqué, vous appréciez le travail en équipe et savez évoluer dans des environnements industriels exigeants, avec une forte culture de la sécurité.
### Ce qui fera la différence ###
Votre **expérience industrielle, votre formation ATEX obligatoire, votre maîtrise technique et votre connaissance des normes suisses** seront vos principaux atouts pour réussir dans ce poste.

C'est le cœur du poste. Il faut savoir le faire seul, dès l'entrée.
2.1 Installation et raccordement
· Pose et raccordement des tableaux : coffrets AC, TGBT, protections, DDR, parafoudres, sectionnements, appareils de mesure.
· Tirage et raccordement des câbles de puissance, dimensionnement contrôlé sur site, chemins de câbles, passages coupe-feu.
· Mise à terre et liaisons équipotentielles : réalisation et vérification.
· Raccordement au point d'injection, coordination avec le GRD, pose et paramétrage des compteurs et du comptage de production.
· Reprise et modification d'installations existantes : identification des circuits, coupures planifiées, remise en service.
2.2 Conduite autonome d'un chantier AC
Un chantier AC confié doit revenir fini, mesuré et documenté.
· Lire le dossier technique, relever ce qui manque et clarifier avant de démarrer.
· Établir la liste de matériel complète et la transmettre à temps pour la commande.
· Planifier son propre travail : ordre des étapes, durées, coordination avec les autres corps de métier et avec le chef de projet.
· Organiser les moyens nécessaires : accès, échafaudage, nacelle, coupures, autorisations d'accès.
· Encadrer ponctuellement un apprenti ou un monteur sur la partie AC.
· Tenir le rapport journalier, les heures et les photos d'avancement.
· Signaler immédiatement tout écart de délai, de coût ou de faisabilité - le plus tôt possible.
2.3 Mesures, sécurité et documents
Sans documents, le chantier n'est pas fini.
· Contrôle propre de l'installation selon la NIBT et l'OIBT.
· Protocoles de mesure complets : continuité du conducteur de protection, résistance d'isolement, impédance de boucle, courant de court-circuit, contrôle des DDR, ordre des phases, mesure de terre.
· Établissement du rapport de sécurité et des annexes, dans les délais et sans reprise.
· Respect des règles de sécurité au travail : cinq règles de sécurité, consignation, EPI, travail sous tension interdit sauf procédure.
· Signalement des non-conformités constatées sur les installations existantes rencontrées.

s.h: 3. PARTIE DC, MISE EN SERVICE ET MONITORING - SOUHAITÉE
s.t:
Souhaitée à l'entrée, indispensable à terme. Si elle n'est pas acquise, elle se forme chez nous - voir chapitre 6.
3.1 Côté DC
· Câblage des strings, connectique, coffrets DC, sectionneurs, parafoudres, cheminements et fixations.
· Contrôle des strings avant mise sous tension : polarité, tension à vide, résistance d'isolement, courant de court-circuit.
· Mesure de courbe I-V et interprétation ; recherche de défaut de string, de défaut d'isolement et d'arc.
· Thermographie de contrôle et lecture des résultats.
3.2 Mise en service des onduleurs
· Mise en service et paramétrage des onduleurs string et centraux : réglages réseau, courbes de puissance, limitation d'injection, protection de découplage.
· Paramétrage conforme aux exigences du GRD et aux prescriptions de raccordement en vigueur.
· Rédaction du protocole de mise en service et du relevé des paramètres appliqués.
· Diagnostic et traitement des défauts d'onduleur, échange sous garantie, relation avec le support fabricant.
3.3 Monitoring et informatique
· Installation et configuration du monitoring : passerelles, compteurs, capteurs, bus de communication (Modbus RTU/TCP, RS485), sondes d'irradiation et de température.
· Mise en réseau : adressage IP, VLAN, routeur 4G, VPN, ports, pare-feu côté client - savoir dialoguer avec un service informatique.
· Contrôle de la remontée des données, alarmes et seuils, création des accès client.
· Analyse d'un écart de production : distinguer un défaut d'installation, un défaut de matériel, un ombrage et une erreur de paramétrage.

s.h: 4. GROSSE PUISSANCE, BORNES ET BATTERIES - ATOUTS
s.t:
Non exigés à l'entrée, mais ce sont les domaines en croissance chez GTS. Une expérience dans l'un d'eux est un vrai plus.
Installations 500 kVA
· Tableaux de puissance, jeux de barres, câbles de forte section, raccordements sur transformateur.
· Sélectivité, coordination des protections, protection de découplage, contrôle de la qualité de réseau.
· Coordination avec le GRD sur les conditions de raccordement et les essais de conformité.
Bornes de recharge
· Installation, raccordement et mise en service de bornes AC et DC.
· Gestion dynamique de charge, délestage, comptage, communication et supervision (OCPP).
· Coordination avec la puissance disponible du bâtiment et l'autoconsommation PV.
Stockage batterie
· Installation, raccordement et mise en service de systèmes de stockage.
· Paramétrage des modes de fonctionnement : autoconsommation, écrêtage, alimentation de secours.
· Exigences de sécurité et de protection incendie applicables aux locaux de batteries.
Large autonomie sur le terrain, cadre clair sur ce qui engage l'entreprise.

· L'organisation de son chantier AC et l'ordre des étapes.
· Les choix de mise en œuvre, dans le respect des plans, de la NIBT et des règles de l'art.
· La liste de matériel et les besoins en moyens de chantier, transmis pour commande.
· L'arrêt d'une opération si les conditions de sécurité ne sont pas réunies - sans discussion ni justification ultérieure.

s.h: Propose, le chef de projet décide
s.t:
· Toute modification du périmètre, du matériel prévu ou de la solution technique.
· Tout travail supplémentaire demandé par le client sur le chantier.
· Tout engagement de délai ou de prix envers un client ou un tiers.

Du nimmst neue Anlagen in Betrieb und integrierst sie in das bestehende Wärmeverteilnetz der Stadt Zürich.
## Aufgaben ##
* Nach einer umfassenden Einarbeitung bist du für die Fehlerortung und Störungssuche in den Wärmeverteilnetzen der Stadt Zürich verantwortlich.
* Du wertest die Messresultate der installierten Leckage-Rechner im Netz aus und beurteilst diese.
* Neue Anlagen nimmst du in Betrieb und integrierst sie in das bestehende Wärmeverteilnetz der Stadt Zürich
* Du verwaltest und archivierst die relevanten technischen Unterlagen, Rapporte und Protokolle und sorgst dafür, dass alle Dokumente immer auf dem neuesten Stand sind.
* In den Fernwärmekammern führst du Elektroinstallationen, Änderungen und Reparaturen selbstständig aus. Zudem erledigst du sachlich begrenzte Elektroinstallationsarbeiten im Niederspannungsbereich.
## Profil ##
* Du hast eine abgeschlossene Grundausbildung als Elektroinstallateur\*in auf Stufe EFZ und verfügst über die Berechtigung nach NIV Art. 13 oder bist bereit, diese zu erwerben.
* Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Betrieb oder Unterhalt bringst du mit.
* Du bist selbstständig und verantwortungsbewusst, bezeichnest dich als Teamplayer und informierst proaktiv.
* Gute Deutschkenntnisse und ein sicherer Umgang mit dem Computer zeichnen dich aus.
* Der Führerausweis der Kategorie B hast du in der Tasche und bist bereit, Pikettdienst zu leisten.
## Wir bieten ##
* Mehr Energie für dein Leben: Durch mobiles Arbeiten, flexible Arbeitsmodelle und Teilzeitmöglichkeiten kannst du deine Arbeitszeit aktiv mitgestalten und sie so einteilen, wie sie am besten zu deinem Leben passt. Du kannst beispielsweise bis zu 2 Wochen zusätzliche Ferien einkaufen und auf allen Stufen Teilzeit arbeiten. Auch Jobsharing/-splitting und unbezahlter Urlaub sind bei uns natürlich möglich.
* Nachhaltig und vergünstigt reisen: Mit dem Mobilitätsbeitrag von bis zu 600 Franken im Jahr reist du günstig und nachhaltig - egal, ob du mit dem Velo durch Zürich radeln oder mit dem Zug die Schweiz erkunden willst.
* Eine Investition in deine Zukunft: Wir legen nicht nur Wert darauf, faire und transparente Löhne zu zahlen, sondern stellen auch sicher, dass dir von deinem Lohn mehr übrigbleibt. Wir übernehmen 60% der Sparbeiträge und bieten zusätzlich einen überobligatorischen Zins auf das angesparte Kapital.
* Ein Energieschub für deine Freizeit: Wir zahlen dir monatlich 100 Franken auf deine Lunch-Check Karte ein. Zudem profitierst du jährlich von weiteren Fringe Benefits im Wert von 150 Franken und von attraktiven Handyabos.
* Entwicklung und Weiterbildung: Mit unserem Talentmanagement fördern wir deine Entwicklung gezielt - durch vielfältige interne und externe Weiterbildungsangebote sowie spannende Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten.
* Sinnhafte Arbeit:-Nachhaltigkeit und sinnstiftende Arbeit sind bei uns nicht nur Worte: Gestalte bei uns Zürich und die Zukunft mit. Setze gemeinsam mit uns Energie für ein gutes Morgen frei.

Stellenbeschreibung
Montage-Elektrikerinnen und Montage-Elektriker sind für die Montage und Installation elektrischer Anlagen in Gebäuden verantwortlich. Zu ihren Aufgaben gehört das Verlegen von Leitungen, das Montieren von Schaltkästen, Schaltern sowie Beleuchtungsanlagen und das Anschliessen von Elektrogeräten.

Darüber hinaus erstellen sie die Verbindungen vom Hausanschluss bis zu den Steckdosen und sorgen dafür, dass alle Installationen den geltenden Sicherheitsvorschriften entsprechen. Diese Position erfordert sowohl technisches Verständnis als auch handwerkliches Geschick, um die verschiedenen Aufgaben effizient und sicher auszuführen.

Montage-Elektriker arbeiten häufig auf Baustellen und müssen in der Lage sein, technische Pläne zu lesen und entsprechend umzusetzen. Teamarbeit und eine sorgfältige Arbeitsweise sind ebenfalls entscheidend, um die Qualität der Installationen zu gewährleisten und die Zufriedenheit der Kunden sicherzustellen.
Anforderungsprofil

· Technische Pläne lesen und verstehen.
· Material und Werkzeuge vorbereiten und bei Bedarf bestellen.
· Material auf der Baustelle lagern und organisieren.
